texts: When a type A tear runs along the greater curve of the arch into the bases of the head vessels, the right repair is total arch replacement with antegrade cerebral perfusion.
A hemi-arch replacement would leave the torn arch and the entry into the head vessels behind, with a high risk of later rupture or redissection.
The head vessels are reattached to the new arch graft, as separate branches or as an island.
Antegrade cerebral perfusion through the axillary or carotid arteries feeds the brain throughout the longer arrest that an arch replacement needs.
In the picture, Franky sews a whole new white arch and re-sews the three necks, while small hoses feed cold water forwards into the lit head lantern.
Memory hook: when the crack reaches the necks, replace the whole arch and feed the head from the front.
